title: An acknowledged ledger commit can be lost on an instance crash under the default IRIS configuration
intended: A revision the ledger reports as committed exists afterwards (spec 213: a revision exists iff its mutations are visible; clients treat the returned revision as durable). No IVG document states a durability premise or the IRIS setting it needs.
observed: Live: with iris.cpf SynchCommit=0 (the IRIS default: TCOMMIT returns before the journal is synced), a 36,000-operation commit acknowledged as seq 3 was entirely absent after a SIGKILL of the container and journal recovery; the ledger stayed consistent (head, revision rows, statement/tuple map, verify equal) and a retry with the same idempotency key committed once. The in-flight trial recovered all-or-nothing.
remedy: Document the durability premise (SynchCommit=1 or a journal flush before acknowledging, or say that acknowledged revisions can be lost on a crash and that an idempotent retry recovers them), and consider checking the setting at enable().
notes: Environment premise rather than a code defect: the engine's documented default permits it. Exactly-once is preserved by the idempotency key; durability is not. The earlier run live-crash-world-r1-invalid exercised two crash/restart cycles without a commit in flight.
